seoTitle: Transfer a Domain From GoDaddy to Squarespace
metaDescription: Move your domain from GoDaddy to Squarespace by connecting it to your site, so your website and domain settings live in one dashboard.
intro: Running a website on Squarespace while your domain sits on a GoDaddy account you barely log into is a common but avoidable headache — renewals, DNS records, and support end up split across two providers instead of one. Squarespace lets you either connect a GoDaddy domain to your site or move it over entirely, and for most people the quicker connect option is all that's needed. This guide follows the real flow across both dashboards: finding your domain in GoDaddy, starting the connection there, and finishing it from Squarespace's own domain settings so your site answers to your existing domain name.

steps.heading: Start from your Squarespace site dashboard
steps.body: Log in to Squarespace and open the site you want the domain attached to. The site's home panel shows setup progress along with quick links, including a "Get a custom domain" button — that's the same destination you'll reach manually through Settings, but it's worth noting here because it confirms your site isn't using a custom domain yet. Have this dashboard open in one tab and your GoDaddy account open in another, since you'll be moving back and forth between the two.

image.caption: A Squarespace site's home dashboard, with a "Get a custom domain" prompt showing the site is still on its default Squarespace URL.

steps.heading: Find the domain in your GoDaddy account
steps.body: In GoDaddy, open My Products and locate the domain you want to use with Squarespace. Each domain listing shows its registration date and registrar, confirming you're looking at the right one before you touch any settings — a small check that matters if your GoDaddy account has more than one domain on it. Click into the domain's management page from here; this is where the connection options live.

image.caption: A domain listed in GoDaddy's account, showing its registration details. Confirm this is the correct domain before starting the connection.

steps.heading: Connect the domain to your Squarespace site
steps.body: From the domain's management page in GoDaddy, use the option to connect it to an existing website rather than starting a full registrar transfer — GoDaddy calls this connecting or forwarding your site. This points the domain's traffic at Squarespace without moving the actual registration, which is faster and avoids the waiting period that comes with a true transfer. GoDaddy handles the technical DNS changes on its end once you confirm.

steps.heading: Add the domain as a third-party domain in Squarespace
steps.body: Back in Squarespace, open Settings, then Domains & Email, and choose the option to use a domain you already own. You'll be prompted to type in the exact domain name — for example, yoursite.com — and Squarespace checks it against what it can see from GoDaddy's side. This is the step that actually links the two accounts together, so double-check the spelling before submitting; a typo here just returns an error rather than connecting anything.

image.caption: The "Use a Domain I Own" panel in Squarespace's Domains & Email settings, where you type in the exact domain name to connect.

steps.heading: Confirm the domain from Squarespace's account menu
steps.body: You can also reach domain management from the account menu in the top navigation, which lists Account Dashboard, Domains, and Log Out — a shortcut worth knowing if you ever need to jump straight to domain settings without digging through Settings again. Squarespace's own site navigation separates Domains from Ecommerce and Marketing, which is a useful reminder that domain connections are handled independently from anything you sell on the site.

image.caption: Squarespace's navigation, with Domains listed both under the account menu and as its own section — a second path to the same settings.

steps.heading: Wait for propagation and verify the connection
steps.body: DNS changes don't take effect instantly — it can take anywhere from a few minutes to a few hours for the domain to fully point at Squarespace, depending on your previous settings and GoDaddy's propagation time. Avoid making further changes on either side while you wait, since stacking edits on top of an unpropagated change is a common cause of confusing errors. Once it resolves, load the domain directly in a browser to confirm it lands on your Squarespace site rather than a GoDaddy parking page.

steps.heading: Troubleshoot with GoDaddy support if it doesn't connect
steps.body: If the domain still isn't resolving to Squarespace after propagation should have finished, GoDaddy's support team can check the DNS records from their side by phone, text, or chat — most connection issues trace back to a leftover DNS record from before you started, which GoDaddy can spot and clear faster than guessing on your own.

faq.question: Do I need to fully transfer the domain, or can I just connect it?
faq.answer: Squarespace supports connecting a third-party domain from GoDaddy without a full registrar transfer, which is the quicker route shown in this guide and enough for most sites.

faq.question: Why would I move a domain from GoDaddy to Squarespace?
faq.answer: Connecting or registering your domain through Squarespace centralizes your website and domain settings instead of juggling two separate provider dashboards for renewals and DNS.

faq.question: How long does it take for the domain to start working?
faq.answer: DNS propagation typically takes anywhere from a few minutes to a few hours after you connect the domain, though it can occasionally take longer depending on prior settings.

faq.question: What if I run into an issue during the connection?
faq.answer: Contact GoDaddy Support by phone, text, or chat — most connection problems come down to a leftover DNS record they can identify and remove from their side.

faq.question: Do I need to already own the domain to use this process?
faq.answer: Yes, this guide covers connecting a domain you've already registered with GoDaddy. Registering a brand-new domain through Squarespace is a separate process.
